verdict.headline: Oil crosses $100 as Mag 7 sheds $797B in worst session since April 2025
verdict.label: Upgrade clock reset; six of seven regime indicators breached; INTC blowout is the lone AI infrastructure positive
verdict.rationale_short: Brent crude crossing $100 per barrel for the first time since May 26 — driven by tanker strikes off the Saudi coast and Trump's civilian-infrastructure ultimatum — sent the 10-year Treasury yield above 4.7% (highest since January 2025) and September rate hike probability to 82%, triggering a $797 billion Magnificent Seven selloff and SPX's worst session since April 2025. The morning's upgrade cycle is fully reset: VIX re-breached 17 to approximately 19.4 and SPX closed at 7,408 — below the 7,480 upgrade threshold and 28 points above the 7,380 formal BEARISH conversion level. Intel's after-hours blowout — revenue $16.1B against a $14.4B consensus, EPS $0.42 against a $0.22 estimate, stock up 12% — is the session's counterweight, validating enterprise AI demand; the directional call entering FOMC week is defensive: protect capital until July 29 FOMC language either closes or extends the September hike thesis.

trade_setups.thesis: Intel reported Q2 revenue of $16.13B (+25% YoY) against a $14.42B consensus, non-GAAP EPS of $0.42 against $0.22 expected, Data Center & AI segment +59% YoY, Q3 revenue guided to $16.3B midpoint — every significant metric exceeded. This is the clearest validation that enterprise AI demand extends beyond hyperscaler capex commitments into broad data-center upgrade cycles. Apple and Microsoft confirmed as 18A foundry partners. Stock is up 12% to approximately $116 in after-hours, establishing a new post-earnings base.

bear_case: Counter-thesis: SPX at 7,408.30 is 28 points above the 7,380 level that converts the regime to formal BEARISH — and the session's underlying dynamics (Brent $100 first close since May 26, 10Y at 4.73% highest since January 2025, September hike probability 82%, VIX re-breach to 19.4, Mag 7 losing $797 billion in a single day) are all moving in the direction that closes that 28-point gap. Tesla's 14.52% collapse on record delivery volumes and negative FCF is not a company-specific story; it is the first clear evidence that the consumer-facing AI economy cannot sustain the current cost structure while simultaneously absorbing a 5.188% 30-year Treasury yield, $100 Brent oil, and a September rate hike trajectory the market is pricing at 82%. Google's -7% on a Cloud 82% beat demonstrates that even the strongest AI-demand numbers cannot offset the multiple compression that $195-205B capex commitments (with more pledged in 2027) create when discount rates are rising. Intel's blowout is the lone bull argument — but enterprise data-center spending confirmations are a 12-18 month revenue story; the FOMC meets in six days, Brent is at $100 today, and the current regime breach count of 6/7 is the highest of this briefing series. If SPX closes below 7,380 at any point before FOMC July 29, the formal BEARISH regime activates. Bear case invalidation: FOMC July 29 statement explicitly closes the door on September language (September hike probability falls below 50%), Brent retreats below $90 on ceasefire signal, and Intel's Q3 guidance of $16.3B mid-range is confirmed as AI-demand durable. All three together would reopen the upgrade cycle; any one alone is insufficient.
